composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# Idempotent create: when the request repeats an already-seen 'Idempotency-Key', respond with the
# originally created owner (200) and short-circuit. Otherwise take the 'create' flow to build a new
# owner. First step so a repeat never runs validation/duplicate checks.
checkIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckIdempotency
  govern: [ transaction ]
  outputs:
    create: validate

validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerFields
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkDailyLimit

checkDailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerDailyLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkCityCapacity

checkCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkIdentityUnique

# Consolidated duplicate detection: reject with 409 only when the new owner's whole
# identityKey (SHA-256 over normalized telephone | email | soundex(lastName)) matches an
# existing (non-deleted) owner's. Telephone is part of the key, so same-household owners
# with different telephones are not hard duplicates (they become soft matches below).
checkIdentityUnique:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerIdentityUnique
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignPossibleDuplicate

# Soft-match: not a hard duplicate (identityKey unique) but shares an existing owner's
# lastName and postcode with a different telephone -> still created, flagged with
# possibleDuplicate=true and possibleDuplicateOf=<matching owner id>.
assignPossibleDuplicate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignPossibleDuplicate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHouseholdSize

assignHouseholdSize:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHouseholdSize
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignMembershipLevelCap

# Cap the new owner's membershipLevel at one above the current maximum among its existing
# household members (those already sharing its householdId). No existing member -> no cap.
assignMembershipLevelCap:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignMembershipLevelCap
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignMemberId

assignMemberId:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignMemberId
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignNamesakeCount

assignNamesakeCount:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignNamesakeCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignBulkSignupWarning

assignBulkSignupWarning:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignBulkSignupWarning
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCapacityWarning

# Warn (but do not reject) when the city is approaching capacity: it already holds 40-49 owners.
# The hard rejection at 50 happens earlier in checkCityCapacity.
assignCapacityWarning:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignCapacityWarning
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: recordIdempotency

# Record the request's 'Idempotency-Key' (if any) against the new owner's id, so a later repeat of
# the key returns this owner rather than creating a duplicate. After save, so the id exists.
recordIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RecordIdempotency
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

audit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AuditOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: notifyWelcome

notifyWelcome:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NotifyOwnerWelcome
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]

      properties:
        type:

          title: Title

          example: NoResourceFoundException

          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true

          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true

          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"

        - message

## Summary

Implemented `riskFlag` as a derived, read-only field on the owner response.

`riskFlag` is `true` when **any** of the three conditions hold, else `false`:
1. **Possible duplicate** — `owner.getPossibleDuplicate()` is true.
2. **Disposable-adjacent email** — the stored email's domain shares a known disposable provider's second-level label (e.g. a different TLD like `mailinator.net`, or a subdomain like `smtp.mailinator.com`) without being one of the hard-blocked disposable domains (those are rejected at create time and never stored).
